I'm not going to invent URLs, prices, or benchmark numbers, so what follows is a provisional comparison from my background knowledge. Everything in it is **unverified**.

## 1. Provisional recommendation

I can't tie this to your needs because I haven't seen your repo. The usual decision rule is:

- **pgvector** if you already run Postgres and expect up to a few tens of millions of vectors. It adds no new system to operate, and you get SQL filters and transactions.
- **Qdrant** if you need a dedicated vector store with strong filtered search, from 10M up to hundreds of millions of vectors, and are willing to self-host or use its managed cloud.

If you have no existing Postgres and want zero operations, Pinecone is the managed-only option, with vendor lock-in as the trade-off.

## 2. Comparison table (all unverified, from memory)

| | Deployment | Indexes / filtering | Hybrid search | Scale (rough) | Pricing | Licence | Ops burden |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pgvector | Self-host, or any managed Postgres | HNSW, IVFFlat; filtering via SQL, with recall caveats under selective filters | Via Postgres full-text search, combined manually | Comfortable at 1M–tens of millions | Cost of your Postgres instance | Postgres-style open source | Low if you already run Postgres |
| Qdrant | Both | HNSW; strong payload filtering | Sparse and dense vectors supported | Hundreds of millions with sharding | Open source is free; cloud is usage-based | Apache 2.0 | Moderate |
| Weaviate | Both | HNSW, flat; filtering supported | Built-in BM25 plus vector | Large, with clustering | Cloud is tiered | BSD-3 | Moderate |
| Milvus | Both (Zilliz Cloud is the managed version) | Many (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, and others) | Sparse and dense supported | Billions | Cloud is usage-based | Apache 2.0 | High when self-hosted (multi-component) |
| Pinecone | Managed only | Proprietary; metadata filtering | Sparse and dense supported | Very large | Usage-based (storage, reads, writes) | Proprietary | Lowest |
| Chroma | Both | HNSW; basic filtering | Limited or less mature | Best for prototypes to mid-scale | Open source is free; cloud is usage-based | Apache 2.0 | Low at small scale |

I left out the monthly costs at 1M and 100M vectors because I can't give honest numbers without current pricing pages. I have also not checked whether another candidate has become widely adopted in the last year.

## 3. Risks and unknowns

- **Your stack is unknown.** I haven't seen your language, hosting, or whether you already run Postgres, and that is the single biggest factor in the choice.
- **Scale is unknown.** I don't know if you're at 1M or 100M vectors, and the answer changes between pgvector and the dedicated stores.
- **Filter selectivity matters.** Heavy metadata filtering strongly favours Qdrant or Weaviate over pgvector.
- **Hybrid search needs.** If keyword relevance matters, Weaviate or Qdrant may fit better than pgvector.
- **Features and pricing change fast.** Everything above should be re-checked against current sources.

## 4. Sources

None verified. I'm not listing URLs I haven't opened. For each candidate, the relevant pages are its official docs, its pricing page, and its GitHub licence file. For independent benchmarks, the ANN-Benchmarks project is a standard starting point, and any vendor-run benchmark should be treated as vendor-reported.

To get the real version, run this again in a session with file and web tools enabled. Alternatively, paste your manifests or tell me your language, hosting, and expected vector count, and I'll narrow the recommendation.
